catalog_entry.label: KenPom rating rank snapshot
contract_types: Men's College Basketball KenPom Top Ratings
catalog_entry.target: Team's rank on the KenPom ratings at a fixed timestamp (exact rank or top-N)
catalog_entry.mechanism: The outcome is the position of a team in a deterministic efficiency-margin list recomputed from all D1 results. It moves only through games played before the snapshot, each shifting AdjEM by the beat-the-expected-margin amount weighted by one over games played, so the probability is an order-statistic crossing problem set by AdjEM gaps, remaining games, update sensitivity and the page's exact reading time.

inputs.why: Direct replication and forward projection of the KenPom list to the snapshot time; the contract is literally a rank in that list.
Stored daily snapshots give the starting ranks and the realised daily rank volatility without retroactive revision.
Rank is an order statistic, so the AdjEM gap to the neighbouring ranks at the cutoff decides how easily results flip it.
Converts each remaining game's margin and opponent into an AdjEM change, the only way a rank can move.
Defines which games are counted at 12:00pm on Mar 15, 2027 and which timezone and refresh the page uses.
Offensive component of the rating being ranked; needed to replicate AdjEM and to project future game efficiency.
Defensive component of the rating being ranked; needed to replicate AdjEM and project future game efficiency.
Margin per possession is scaled by possessions, and tempo shifts how far one game moves AdjEM.
Fundamentals-only ensemble supplies win probabilities and margins for the remaining games without betting lines.
Byes, bracket size and neutral sites fix how many games each team plays before the snapshot.
Blowout versus competitive regimes determine how margins translate into the efficiency the algorithm sees.
Late-season absences change expected efficiency in the final games before the snapshot.
Connectivity and sample size set how noisy the replicated rating is near the cutoff.
Versioned wording fixes the ratings page, timestamp and what Yes means.
Settled value and time show which page state the exchange actually read.

interactions.hypothesis: A flip needs the per-game update to be large relative to the AdjEM gap, so the same remaining schedule is safe for a team with a wide gap and live for a bunched one.

Extra tournament games add variance to a high-rated team's rank because the rating only falls if it under-performs its expected margin, and bye teams carry less variance than teams that must play three games.
Blowout margins earn diminishing rating credit, so heavy favourites gain little from beating weak conference-tournament opponents while narrow wins can still cost rating.

contract.settlement_definition: Yes settles if the named team holds exactly rank 1 (KXNCAAMBKENPOMRANK, rank given in the ticker) or is ranked 25 or better (KXNCAAMBKENPOMTOP) on the 2027 Pomeroy College Basketball Ratings page as shown on Mar 15, 2027 at 12:00pm EST; resolution rests solely on that KenPom page at that instant, so games completed after the page state do not count.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolution is determined solely by the KenPom ratings on Mar 15, 2027 at 12:00pm EST.
rules_evidence.establishes: The ratings page at a fixed timestamp is the only source of truth; no later revision or other ranking source is considered.

rules_evidence.quote: If Xavier is ranked top 25 on the 2027 Pomeroy College Basketball Ratings on Mar 15, 2027 at 12:00pm EST, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The top-N variant is a threshold on rank (25 or better) in the Pomeroy ratings at the same timestamp.

variants_and_edge_cases: Exact-rank markets (#1 sampled; other rank values may exist in the series) resolve on one slot, while top-25 is a threshold; the same team can be close to one and far from the other.
The label 12:00pm EST falls the day after US daylight time begins in 2027; whether it means 12:00 fixed-offset EST or New York clock time is not stated in the sampled rules.
Rules do not say what happens if the site is unavailable at the timestamp, if the ranking is mid-refresh, or how tied ranks are shown; the sample is silent.
Season label '2027' ratings refer to the 2026-27 season; games on Mar 15 itself that finish after the page state are not counted.
contract.settlement_data_source: KenPom (kenpom.com) Pomeroy College Basketball Ratings page read at Mar 15, 2027 12:00pm EST; paywalled single-operator source with no public API.

mechanism.summary: The outcome is a rank in an algorithmic list, not a vote. KenPom ranks all D1 teams by adjusted efficiency margin, a running opponent- and venue-adjusted points-per-100-possessions margin computed from every game so far. A rank on Mar 15 is therefore (1) the current rating state, plus (2) the games each team still plays before noon on that date, which depends on the regular-season finale and conference-tournament survival, plus (3) the update each result causes, which is small late in the season because each game carries about one over games played weight and which rewards beating the expected margin, not winning, plus (4) the order-statistic mapping from AdjEM values to a rank where local density at the cutoff decides how fragile a position is, and (5) the exact reading of the page at the timestamp. The #1 contract is a single-slot race between a few teams; top-25 is a boundary-crossing problem against a bunched cluster.

stages.name: Starting rating state
stages.description: The KenPom list at pricing time is a deterministic function of every D1 result so far: per-team adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency per 100 possessions, tempo, and opponent adjustment solved jointly across the connected schedule. The starting rank, the AdjEM level and the gap to neighbouring ranks are therefore observable by anyone with the paywalled data or a good replica such as Torvik's T-Rank. Early in the season preseason priors still carry weight; by March the rating is almost entirely results.
stages.distribution: Near-continuous AdjEM values; the rank is a discrete order statistic with local density that is high around #25 and thin at the top.

stages.name: Games still to be played
stages.description: Between pricing and noon on Mar 15 each team plays its regular-season finale and, if it qualifies, conference-tournament games. The count is set by format, byes, seed, and elimination: a conference favourite may play three games, a bubble team may play one and exit. Each game's outcome and margin come from the matchup of the two teams' strengths, venue and who is available, with the usual single-game noise of about 10 points of margin.
stages.distribution: Number of games is a small integer random variable (0 to 4) with a heavy dependence on bracket survival; per-game margin is roughly normal with sd near 10 to 11 points and fatter tails from blowouts.

stages.name: Result to rating update
stages.description: Each completed game feeds the algorithm as an adjusted efficiency margin: points per 100 possessions relative to what the opponent usually allows, adjusted for venue, then blended into the team's running rating with a weight of roughly one over the games played and some recency emphasis. Opponents move too, so a win over a team that then collapses is worth less. Blowout margins are treated with diminishing returns, so running up the score gains little and a close win over a weak team can lower the rating.
stages.distribution: Per-game rating change is mean-near-zero with sd of a few tenths of AdjEM late in the season; the sign depends on beating the expected margin rather than winning, giving a concave response to margin.

stages.name: Rank as an order statistic
stages.description: The settled quantity is the position of one team among about 360 AdjEM values after all updates. For an exact-rank contract the team must hold one specific position, so both its own movement and the movement of every neighbour matter and the probability is a thin slice. For top-25 the team must sit above the AdjEM of the 25th-26th boundary, so a bunched cluster makes flips likely. Ties in displayed rating are unlikely at two decimals but possible in rank ordering rules unknown to us.
stages.distribution: Probability mass is concentrated within a few ranks of the current position; exact-rank markets are far more concentrated and discrete than threshold markets, which behave like normal-tail crossing probabilities.

stages.name: Snapshot reading and settlement
stages.description: Resolution reads the ratings page at 12:00pm EST on Mar 15, 2027 and nothing else. Which games are processed by then, when the site refreshes, the EST versus daylight-time labelling and any mid-year methodology change decide the exact list used. KenPom is a single-operator paywalled site, so there is no formal feed and the Kalshi settlement source is whatever the page shows at that instant.
stages.distribution: Mostly deterministic once the page is read, but with a small probability of timing or refresh mismatches that flip teams sitting at a boundary.

cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.label: KenPom AdjEM gap density around the target rank
cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.mechanism: A rank contract is decided by the order statistics of ~360 AdjEM values; what matters is the AdjEM distance to the neighbouring ranks, not the absolute rating.
cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.rationale: Near #25 teams are separated by a few tenths of a point of AdjEM while near #1 the gap can be a point or more, so identical rating noise moves a top-25 contract far more than a #1 contract. A team at #40 can be closer to the line in expected moves than a team at #28 if the intermediate teams are bunched.
cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.measurement: At each daily snapshot sort AdjEM and compute for the target team gap_up = AdjEM(rank r-1) - AdjEM(team) and gap_down = AdjEM(team) - AdjEM(rank r+1), plus the number of teams within +/-0.5 AdjEM. Divide each gap by sigma_move = sqrt(games_left) * per-game AdjEM change sd (from cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity) to get a z-distance to a flip. For top-25 use the gap between AdjEM of the 25th and 26th teams. As-of: last snapshot before pricing, recomputed each day.
raw_data: daily AdjEM for all D1 teams
cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.why: Turns a rank threshold into a distance-to-flip in standard deviations, which is the quantity that separates a safe top-25 team from a coin flip.

cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.label: Per-game AdjEM update sensitivity
cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.mechanism: KenPom's rating is a running opponent-adjusted efficiency margin, so one game moves it by (game-level adjusted margin minus current rating) weighted by 1/games played, with opponent strength and venue entering the game-level number.
cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.rationale: Late in the season each game carries a weight near 1/30 to 1/35, so a team can move only a few tenths per game, and the move is zero in expectation when the team performs at its rating; the algorithm weights recent games and its blowout treatment are not public, which is the subtle part.
cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.measurement: Fit on daily snapshot pairs from the prior three seasons: dAdjEM_team,t = w(g) * (adjusted game margin per 100 possessions - AdjEM_t-1) + opponent-feedback term, with g games played; estimate w(g), a recency multiplier, and a blowout cap by least squares. Output expected move and sd per game as a function of g, opponent AdjEM and location. Validate: out-of-sample RMSE of next-day AdjEM below 0.15. As-of: snapshots before the game.
cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.why: The only route by which a rank moves between now and Mar 15 runs through this per-game update, so its size and variance set the probability of crossing a cutoff.

cbb.kenpom_snapshot_timing_rules.label: KenPom snapshot timing and counting rules
cbb.kenpom_snapshot_timing_rules.mechanism: The contract reads the ratings page at 12:00pm 'EST' on Mar 15, 2027, so which games have been processed, the daily refresh time and whether the label EST means a fixed offset or the local New York clock decide the exact state.
cbb.kenpom_snapshot_timing_rules.rationale: Mar 15, 2027 falls after US daylight time starts (Mar 14, 2027), so literal EST would be 1pm Eastern daylight time; Selection Sunday conference finals may be unfinished at noon; the page may refresh only overnight. Any of these can swap which games count for a bubble-of-the-list team.
cbb.kenpom_snapshot_timing_rules.measurement: Record for every past season the observed refresh timestamps of the ratings page (daily capture every 30 minutes from 04:00 to 14:00 ET), the last completed game included, and the games on the target date that start before noon. Compute n_games_pending_at_snapshot per team and a flag for mid-update states. Resolve the EST/EDT ambiguity by capturing both the 11:00 and 12:00 ET page. As-of: captured live on the date.
free_sources: own_capture of the KenPom page (requires subscription)
NCAA schedule listings for tip times
cbb.kenpom_snapshot_timing_rules.why: Defines exactly which results are in the list when the exchange reads it, which matters most for teams with a game on the morning of the snapshot.

cbb.adj_off.reason: A component of AdjEM; useful for replicating the rating and projecting future game efficiency, but the contract is on the net, so it is not primary.

cbb.adj_def.reason: The defensive component of AdjEM, needed for replication and matchup projection; the net rating is what is ranked.

cbb.tempo.reason: Possessions scale the margin that enters the per-100 rating, and tempo changes how a given points margin converts to AdjEM.

cbb.ratings_fundamentals.reason: Provides forward win probabilities and expected margins for remaining games without betting lines; the list itself still comes from replication.

cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.reason: Fixes how many games each team can still play before the snapshot, which controls the amount of rating variance left.

cbb.margin_regime_mixture.reason: The algorithm's blowout treatment makes the margin regime relevant to how much rating a result is worth.

cbb.injuries.reason: An absence shifts expected efficiency in the last few games only; the effect on the rating is lagged and small.

cbb.rating_uncertainty.reason: KenPom's displayed rating has no uncertainty by construction; the input only helps quantify replication error and early-season prior weight, which is minor by March.

interactions.mechanism: A rank flips only when the cumulative AdjEM move of the team and its neighbours exceeds the local gap. The probability behaves like a normal-tail crossing in the ratio of gap to per-game update sd times root games left, so risk is low until the ratio falls below about 1.
interactions.how_to_test: Build z = gap / (sd_game * sqrt(games_left)) per team-day and check that realised flip frequency over prior seasons is a steep logistic in z, with a clear knee near z of 1.

interactions.mechanism: A first-round bye removes one or two games, so a bye team's rank variance is smaller; a top seed that is knocked out early loses little rating if it still performed close to expectation, whereas deep runs add variance in both directions.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare day-to-day rank change sd over Mar 8-15 between bye and non-bye top-40 teams in past seasons, conditioning on games played in the window.

interactions.mechanism: Because large margins are discounted by the algorithm, a high-offence team that wins by 30 gains much less than 3 times the credit of a 10-point win, so projected AdjEM gains from soft opponents are muted and a close win can reduce AdjEM.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress next-day dAdjEM on margin versus expected margin with a spline; the slope should flatten beyond about 15 to 20 points above expectation.

interactions.mechanism: A key player's absence lowers true strength immediately, but the rating reflects it only after games are played without him, so a team's rank on Mar 15 can lag its true strength; the lag matters in bunched regions.
interactions.how_to_test: Event study of teams losing a top-two impact player in the last three weeks: compare AdjEM change over the next 10 days to the lineup-adjusted rating drop.

interactions.mechanism: A team playing on the morning of the snapshot has a chance that its result is or is not processed, and the effect only matters if the team sits within a few tenths of a cutoff, so timing and gap density jointly drive the risk.
interactions.how_to_test: Flag team-days with a game finishing within 6 hours of the capture and measure how often rank at 12:00 differs from rank at the next refresh, split by gap bucket.

nonlinearities.shape: step-like: flip probability near zero until gap falls below about one per-game update sd
nonlinearities.why: Rank changes need an actual crossing of neighbouring AdjEM values, so risk is a sharply nonlinear function of gap and clusters of teams within half a point multiply it.
Each game carries less weight as the season lengthens, so by mid-March the same blowout moves AdjEM roughly half as much as in January.

nonlinearities.shape: concave in points margin beyond expectation
nonlinearities.why: The algorithm discounts garbage-time and very large margins, so rating credit saturates while the downside for a poor performance does not.

catalog_entry.label: CBB race to N points
contract_types: Men's College Basketball Race to Points
Men's College Basketball Race to 10 Points
Men's College Basketball Race to 25 Points
Men's College Basketball Race to 50 Points
catalog_entry.target: Which team first reaches N points in a game (first-passage event)
catalog_entry.mechanism: Each team's points arrive in discrete possession-by-possession chunks produced by the starting units, so the race is a first-passage problem on two alternating scoring processes. The edge comes from the opening five's points per possession, the opening possession tie-break, early turnovers and rebounds, and N, which scales luck versus rating: races to 10 are mostly variance, races to 50 approach the share of points over about 26 minutes.

inputs.why: Team opening-segment scoring profile and opening-possession edge, the closest direct predictor of a first-passage race.
First-passage simulation on alternating possessions with tip-win edge, specific to a first-to-N contract.
Scales the edge by N because races to 10, 25 and 50 weigh luck and rating differently.
Opponent-adjusted offence sets points per possession for the team's unit in the race.
Opponent-adjusted defence sets the points per possession the rival unit concedes in the race.
Opening five and their health decide who is on the floor in the race segment before substitutions.
Late scratches change the starting lineup and thus scoring rate in the opening minutes.
Starter-unit on-floor efficiency is the actual scoring rate in the race window.
Possessions per minute fix how fast the points accumulate and how many tries each side gets.
Early-game pace relative to full game captures slow starts or quick openings by team.
Early three-point reliance drives a scoring distribution with lumpy 3-point jumps and fat tails.
Home court shapes opening-segment scoring through crowd and shooting familiarity.
Bonus and foul counts matter for the race to 50 where free throws may arrive before halftime.
Play-by-play ordering errors can flip close races and settlement lag affects resolution.
Wording defines the first to score N, game original date and postponement window.
Postponement and 48-hour rule decide whether a market resolves or goes to fair price.

interactions.hypothesis: The opening-possession tie-break matters most when both starting units score at similar rates, and it fades when one unit's points per possession clearly exceeds the other's.
A starting-lineup change inside the race window moves the unit's scoring rate more than the season rating suggests, so lineup news interacts with unit efficiency.
The same offensive gap converts into a larger race advantage at N=50 than at N=10 because the signal accumulates linearly while noise grows with the square root of possessions.

contract.settlement_definition: Yes settles if the named team is the first to score N points (the sampled strike is 10) in the specified men's college basketball game originally scheduled on the stated date; the market is per team, a game postponed but starting within 48 hours remains open and settles on the official result, and a game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves all markets to a fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: If Virginia is the first to score 10 points in the Arkansas vs Virginia men's college basketball game originally scheduled for Nov 8, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: The racing entity is a team and the event is the first team to reach 10 points, tied to the game's original scheduled date.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start, all markets will resolve to a fair price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Cancelled or long-postponed games resolve at fair price rather than Yes or No.

variants_and_edge_cases: The sampled rules text exists only for KXNCAAMBRACE (strike 10); KXNCAAMBFIRST10, KXNCAAMBFIRST25 and KXNCAAMBFIRST50 are TITLE_ONLY with no sampled rules or listings, so their entity, ties and overtime handling are unverified.

A team may jump past N on a single possession (for example from 8 to 11 with a three); the sample does not say whether reaching or exceeding N counts, though reaching at least N is the natural reading.
N=50 can be reached only after halftime for slow teams, and for very low-scoring games it may be reached in overtime or never; the sample does not say how a game ending before N is handled.
Both teams' markets in the same game are separate binary contracts so their prices should sum near one.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official play-by-play and final result of the NCAA game (the rules cite the official final result); the specific provider is not named in the sampled text.

mechanism.summary: The outcome is which team's cumulative score hits N first, a first-passage event on two interleaved point-accumulation processes. Points come in discrete amounts (free throws, twos, threes) on possessions that alternate between the teams, so for small N the winner is largely determined by the unit that starts, the tip and opening possession, and a few variance-heavy possessions. As N rises, the rating gap in points per possession accumulates linearly while noise grows with the square root of possessions, so the race approaches the full-game share of scoring, and the identity of the unit shifts from starters to rotation. Team defence matters through the rival's rate, tempo through time but little through relative advantage, and bonus free throws and early fouls matter for the 50-point race. Settlement follows the official scoring sequence.

stages.name: Opening possession and tip
stages.description: The game begins with a jump ball and the winner takes the first possession; the possession arrow then governs later held balls. Because the two teams alternate possessions, the team that starts with the ball is first whenever both need the same number of possessions to reach N. Tip-win probability is near 50 percent pregame with only a small centre-height effect, so this stage is mainly a tie-break and it is known only after tip.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli near 0.5 for the tip, converted into a few points of probability of winning the race; the effect shrinks as N grows from 10 to 50.

stages.name: Starting-unit scoring rate
stages.description: For the first four to ten minutes the players on the floor are the announced starters, so the relevant rate is the points per possession of that five against the opponent's opening five, not the season-long team efficiency that includes bench units and garbage time. Matchup features such as press defence, zone, rim protection and three-point reliance shift the rate, and a late injury changes the opening five.
stages.distribution: Points per possession per trial is discrete (0,1,2,3, sometimes 4) with mean near 1.0 and sd near 1.1, so total points after k possessions has heavy lumpiness; team rates differ by a few tenths of a point per possession.

stages.name: Possession count and continuation
stages.description: The number of possessions in the window depends on pace, the share of turnovers and offensive rebounds that break alternation and how quickly each team shoots. Tempo is shared, but a team that forces early turnovers or crashes the offensive glass gets more tries inside the same stretch of game clock. A slow team facing a fast one can still be pulled into the faster pace early.
stages.distribution: Possessions inside the race window are a small count (about 8 to 12 per team for N=10), nearly equal for both sides with a skew from offensive rebounds and steals.

stages.name: Threshold crossing by N
stages.description: The outcome is a first-passage time: the first team whose cumulative points reach N. A 10-point race ends within roughly the first five minutes and mostly reflects luck; a 25-point race ends near the 10th to 12th minute and starts to separate the better offence; a 50-point race often ends in the second half after halftime and approximates the share of points over about 26 minutes, with foul trouble and bonus free throws mattering for who gets there first.
stages.distribution: Crossing times are discrete with overshoot (a 3-pointer can jump from 8 to 11); variance of the points gap grows like sqrt of possessions, so the favourite's race probability rises with N toward the full-game win probability.

stages.name: Event sequencing and settlement
stages.description: Settlement uses the official sequence of scoring events, with the market tied to the original scheduled game date and a 48-hour postponement window after which markets resolve to a fair price. Close races can depend on the ordering of simultaneous events in the official play-by-play, for example free throws after a shooting foul, and on stat-provider corrections.
stages.distribution: Mostly deterministic once play-by-play is final; small probability of ordering disputes or provider lag, and a small probability of postponement-driven fair-price resolution.

cbb.race_possession_alternation_model.label: Possession-alternation first-passage model
cbb.race_possession_alternation_model.mechanism: Both teams get nearly equal possessions in the opening minutes, so the first to N points is decided by points-per-possession draws on alternating possessions, with ties in possession count broken by who has the ball first.
cbb.race_possession_alternation_model.rationale: With about one point per possession a race to 10 is a 9-to-11 possession event; the team starting with the ball reaches N first whenever both need the same number of possessions, a built-in edge of a few points of probability. Offensive rebounds and turnovers break strict alternation, so the edge shrinks as N grows and with offensive-rebound rate.
cbb.race_possession_alternation_model.measurement: From play-by-play of 5 prior seasons estimate for each team in the opening segment the distribution of points per possession (outcomes 0,1,2,3,4 with free throws), the offensive-rebound continuation rate and opening turnover rate with shrinkage n/(n+15) to the opponent-adjusted conference mean. Simulate 50,000 races for N = 10, 25, 50 with alternating possessions, giving first possession to team A or B; output P(A first to N | possession A) and P(A first | possession B). Mixed with P(tip win) = 0.5 pregame, updated to 1 or 0 once the tip is known. As-of: lineup-confirmed time before tip.
raw_data: play-by-play with scoring sequence and possession flag
cbb.race_possession_alternation_model.why: Gives the first-passage structure of the contract and quantifies the opening-possession edge that no efficiency rating contains.

cbb.race_n_threshold_scaling.label: Race-N threshold scaling and win-link
cbb.race_n_threshold_scaling.mechanism: The mapping from team scoring rate to winning the race changes with N: at 10 it is mostly opening variance, at 25 it is a half-way runs contest, and at 50 it approaches the share of points over about 26 minutes and can span the halftime break.
cbb.race_n_threshold_scaling.rationale: Because sd of the points gap grows like the square root of possessions while the mean grows linearly, the favourite's chance rises with N toward its win probability. A team that wins by defence may lose the race to 50 if it scores slowly, so offence level and not margin is the driver.
cbb.race_n_threshold_scaling.measurement: From historical play-by-play compute for N in {10,25,50} the minute each team reaches N and whether it led the race; fit logit P(race win N) = a_N + b_N * (AdjO_A/AdjD_B-based expected points per possession difference) by N with team-level random effects, and record the median time to N and share of games where N is reached after halftime. As-of: ratings snapshot before tip, five seasons of games.
raw_data: time and score at each scoring event
cbb.race_n_threshold_scaling.why: Shows how much of the pre-game edge carries to each race length, which is needed because the contract comes in 10, 25 and 50-point forms with different variance.

cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.reason: Models the opening-segment unit scoring and the tip edge; a close match to the first-to-N event.

cbb.adj_off.reason: Points per possession of the offence against this opponent is the rate of the race; full-game efficiency is a reasonable but not opening-specific proxy.

cbb.adj_def.reason: Defensive efficiency sets what the rival can score per possession; same full-game proxy caveat.

cbb.starters.reason: The opening lineup is the only unit that matters for a race to 10 and mostly for 25; a bench-heavy opening changes the rate.

cbb.injuries.reason: Matters through the starting five and is time-sensitive, but most of its value is captured in starters once lineups are posted.

cbb.lineups.reason: Five-man unit efficiency estimates the starter unit's scoring rate, though samples per unit are small and noisy.

cbb.tempo.reason: Possessions per minute set time-to-N but both teams share the pace, so it barely changes who gets there first.

cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.reason: Early pace relative to full game is a relevant team trait for an early-game event.

cbb.three_pt_dist.reason: Three-point reliance changes the lumpiness of scoring and the chance of a fast 9-0 start, but it is a distribution input rather than a mean shifter.

cbb.venue.reason: Home-court margin is a full-game effect; its size on the first four minutes is smaller and uncertain.

cbb.half_foul_bonus.reason: Relevant mainly for the 50-point variant, near irrelevant to a race to 10.

cbb.box_score_source_risk.reason: Settlement can depend on the ordering of scoring events in the official play-by-play; probability of error is low but non-zero.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines the settled event; the sample says first to score 10 and a 48-hour postponement window.

m.lifecycle.reason: Postponements and cancellations resolve to fair price rather than win or lose, so timing matters for settlement.

interactions.mechanism: With near-equal points per possession the team with the first possession wins ties in possession count and gains a few percentage points; when one unit's rate is clearly higher the tie-break matters less, so the opening-possession effect depends on the rate gap.
interactions.how_to_test: On historical play-by-play, split races to 10 by first possession and by absolute gap in opening-unit points per possession and compare win rates across gap bins.

interactions.mechanism: If a regular starter is out, the opening unit is a different five with a different scoring rate and the effect is concentrated in the first segment before the usual rotation resumes; the season's team rating understates this for races to 10.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare race-to-10 win rates for teams with a changed starter against baseline, controlling for adjusted offence.

interactions.mechanism: Signal grows with the number of possessions and noise with its square root, so the effect of the offensive rating gap on the race win probability scales with N; at 10 it is slight, at 50 close to the full-game effect.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit logit race win on offence gap by N with an interaction term and check the slope increases monotonically from N=10 to 50.

interactions.mechanism: Three-point heavy teams produce lumpier scores, and in a fast game more of those attempts occur in the window, increasing the chance of an early 9-0 run and spreading the first-passage time distribution.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare variance of points after 6 possessions for high and low three-point rate teams, and condition on pace tercile.

interactions.mechanism: Reaching 50 depends on whether bonus free throws begin before the team gets there; once a team enters the bonus the points per possession rises, which switches the late race regime for teams that foul early.
interactions.how_to_test: For N=50 races, compare crossing times for games where either team entered the bonus before 12:00 of the first half against games where neither did.

nonlinearities.shape: increasing concave in N toward the full-game win probability
nonlinearities.why: Favourite's race probability rises with N because mean accumulates linearly and sd as a square root, but saturates near the pregame win probability.

nonlinearities.shape: tie-break edge decays with N and with offensive-rebound rate
nonlinearities.why: The first-possession edge exists only while strict alternation holds; the more possessions and extra offensive-rebound tries, the more it washes out.

nonlinearities.shape: convex tail in the probability of a 9-0 start
nonlinearities.why: Points come in lumps of 3, so a handful of threes quickly produces a fast opening run and the likelihood of a very early crossing grows convexly with 3-point reliance.

catalog_entry.label: CBB season per-game stat leader
contract_types: Men's College Basketball Conference Stat Leader
catalog_entry.target: Player with the highest season per-game stat (points, threes, etc.) nationally or within a conference, NCAA minimums apply
catalog_entry.mechanism: The winner is the maximum over qualified players of a season-long per-game average accumulated over every official game, postseason included. Each average is minutes times a role-driven per-minute rate with large game-to-game noise, thinned by missed games and gated by NCAA minimum qualification, so the probability depends on talent, role stability, availability, how locked the average already is, and which official table settles it.

inputs.why: Leaderboard max-of-noisy-averages simulation including postseason games and thresholds, the direct model of this contract.
NCAA minimums decide who is eligible, so a leader near the cutoff can be removed from the contest.
Remaining-swing bound shows how locked the leaderboard is given games played and remaining.
Usage and shot share drive points, threes and rebounds per game and persist across games.
Projected minutes scale every counting stat and respond to blowouts, fouls and role.
Injury, suspension and coach decisions reduce games played and can disqualify a candidate.
Postseason and late-season availability risk for the top candidates affects both games and qualification.
Threes made per game is minutes times attempts times a Beta-uncertain make rate, the compound behind the 3PM leader markets.
Three-point attempt volume decides who can lead the made-threes category more than shooting percentage.
Rebounds per game depend on the pool of missed shots and offensive-rebound structure of the team.
Assists per game depend on the potential assists and teammates' make rate, not only the passer.
Transfers and freshmen have no college role history, so the leader pool needs cold-start priors.
Teammate injuries redistribute usage and minutes and can raise a candidate's average.
Per-game sd by role sets how quickly the average converges and how much noise remains.
Counts of games, sites and which are official define the sample size over which the average is built.
Possessions scale the opportunities for counting stats and differ by team across the pool.
Stat provider reliability and correction lag matter for the final official table.
Wording fixes which games count and the minimum thresholds and the non-qualification clause.
Final leader and timing of settlement from past seasons show the lag and source used.

interactions.hypothesis: Minutes and usage multiply, so a modest rise in either lifts the average more than additively, and role changes after teammate departures or injuries move leaders.
Missed games matter as a cliff once a candidate nears the NCAA minimum, so injury risk is far more costly for a leader close to the threshold.
The same gap between candidates is worth more probability late than early because each remaining game moves an average by less, so race uncertainty collapses as games are played.

contract.settlement_definition: Yes settles if the named player records the most of the stated per-game statistic (points per game and made threes per game in the samples) in Division I (KXNCAAMBSTATLEADER) or in a named conference (KXNCAAMBCONFLEADER) over the entire 2026-27 season including the postseason, subject to NCAA minimum qualification thresholds, using all official games and excluding games clearly designated as unofficial exhibitions.

rules_evidence.establishes: Only players meeting the NCAA minimums can win, so eligibility is part of the settled event.

rules_evidence.quote: Exhibition and preseason games that are clearly designated as unofficial do not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: The sample is all official games; unofficial exhibitions are excluded.

rules_evidence.quote: NIT games and games in other official postseason competitions (including the College Basketball Crown, CBI, or CIT, when held) also count.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postseason games beyond the NCAA Tournament, including non-NCAA events, are in the sample.

variants_and_edge_cases: Conference version covers per-game stats of players in one conference across all of their games, including nonconference games, not only conference games.
Categories vary by market (points per game for SEC, made threes per game for national in the samples); other categories such as rebounds or assists were not sampled.
The sampled rules_secondary is truncated at 'If Zoom Diallo does not', so the clause on a non-qualifying or non-playing player is not visible; tie-break treatment is also not visible.
Because postseason games count, the final answer is only known after the last postseason event, and a team's postseason run changes the sample size.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled text; likely the NCAA statistical leaderboards or equivalent official season statistics, to be confirmed.

mechanism.summary: The outcome is the argmax of a set of season-long per-game averages among players who meet NCAA minimums. A player's average equals the mean of his counting stat across all official games he plays, so it is built from minutes, role and usage, per-minute production against opponents and pace, and the count of games he is available for. Game-to-game noise is large relative to true differences between top candidates, so early in the season many players are live, and as games accumulate each new game moves the average less. Availability is a hazard: missed games shrink the sample and can drop a player under the NCAA minimum, which removes him from the contest. Postseason games add samples for deep-run teams. Each stat category has its own driver: scoring by usage, threes by attempts volume, rebounds by the missed-shot pool, assists by teammate shot making. Settlement then reads one official table.

stages.name: Candidate pool and per-game talent
stages.description: The leaderboard starts from who can plausibly lead: high-usage scorers, volume three-point shooters, big men on rebound-rich teams, primary ballhandlers, and rim protectors for blocks. Each candidate has a true per-game mean set by minutes and role, usage, per-minute production and teammates, and many of the best candidates are transfers or freshmen with no college role history, so their means are uncertain and shrunk toward role priors. National contracts have a pool of about 30 credible names; conference contracts have 5 to 10.
stages.distribution: True means are separated by a few tenths to a few points per game among the top candidates; uncertainty about each mean is large for new players and shrinks roughly as 1 over sqrt of games.

stages.name: Per-game production process
stages.description: Each game, a candidate's stat is produced from minutes, shot attempts or rebound and assist opportunities and conversion. For points it is possessions times usage times efficiency plus free throws, for threes made it is attempts times a make rate that is mostly noise, for rebounds it is the missed-shot pool and positioning, for assists it is teammates' shot making. Opponent, pace and game script change a single game's output, so the per-game sd is large relative to differences between candidates.
stages.distribution: Per-game counts are overdispersed and nonnegative; points have sd near 6 to 8, threes made near 1.5 to 2 with Beta-binomial-like tails, so a season average has sd near 1 over sqrt of games times that.

stages.name: Games played, availability and postseason sample
stages.description: The average is taken over all official games the player plays, regular season, conference tournament, NCAA, NIT and other official postseason events, so deep-run teams add games and eliminated teams stop. Injury, suspension, redshirt or coach decisions reduce games played and can end a candidacy; the sampled rules say exhibition and preseason games that are clearly unofficial do not count.
stages.distribution: Games played is a discrete count of about 28 to 38 with a left tail from injuries; missed games are clustered and correlated with team success and with the stage of the season.

stages.name: Qualification filter and race to the maximum
stages.description: Only players who meet the NCAA minimum qualification thresholds are eligible, so the winner is the maximum over the qualified set of final per-game averages. The probability for a candidate is the chance that he qualifies and that his noisy average exceeds all other qualified candidates'. Lead stability grows as games accumulate because each new game changes an average by less, and a candidate within one standard error of the leader still has a live chance.
stages.distribution: The max of several correlated noisy averages with a hard eligibility filter; probabilities concentrate on the top 2 to 4 candidates and the lead probability moves in jumps when a candidate is injured or crosses the threshold.

stages.name: Official table and settlement
stages.description: Settlement uses the player's statistics for the entire season including postseason, from some official or reference table; the sampled text is cut off at the clause about what happens if the named player does not qualify or the leader is tied, so the exact rule is not visible. Lag in official updates, differences between the NCAA site and box scores, and the treatment of non-NCAA postseason events can decide a close race.
stages.distribution: Mostly deterministic given the final table, with a small chance of source disagreement or ties that flips close races.

cbb.stat_leader_qualification_tracker.label: NCAA minimum-qualification tracker for leaderboard eligibility
cbb.stat_leader_qualification_tracker.mechanism: A player leads the official per-game list only if he meets the NCAA minimum (a share of team games or a minimum total of the stat), so a missed-games run turns a leading average into a non-qualifier and removes him from the max.
cbb.stat_leader_qualification_tracker.rationale: Qualification is a cliff, not a slope: a player averaging 24 ppg who has missed too many games is not eligible, while the next qualifying player wins. Thresholds differ by category and are set by the NCAA, and postseason games raise the team-games denominator.
cbb.stat_leader_qualification_tracker.measurement: For each candidate and category compute games_played, team_games_played, projected team games including expected postseason (conference tournament, NCAA, NIT, CBB Crown) and the stat-specific NCAA minimum from the current NCAA statistics rules; the feature is P(qualify) = P(games played over remaining team games >= required share) using the player's per-game availability probability from cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy, and distance in games to the threshold. As-of: recomputed after each team game.
cbb.stat_leader_qualification_tracker.why: Turns a leading average into the right conditional event, since only qualified players can win and a leader near the threshold can drop out.

cbb.stat_leader_source_reconciliation.label: Official stat feed reconciliation and update lag
cbb.stat_leader_source_reconciliation.mechanism: The rules count all official games including non-NCAA postseason events, but the usual leaderboard source may lag, may exclude events such as the College Basketball Crown, and can differ from box scores by stat corrections.
cbb.stat_leader_source_reconciliation.rationale: A season-long contract is settled off one table after the last game; differences of 0.1 to 0.3 per game between sources can decide a close race for threes made or rebounds, and the postseason inclusion list goes beyond NCAA-sanctioned events.
cbb.stat_leader_source_reconciliation.measurement: For the 3 most recent seasons collect the final per-game value for top-20 players in each category from the NCAA site, Sports-Reference and ESPN, and compute the absolute difference, the date each source's table becomes final, and whether Crown, CBI and CIT games were included. Define source_gap_i = max pairwise difference and a flag if the gap between rank 1 and 2 is below it. As-of: refreshed weekly during the season and daily at the end.
cbb.stat_leader_source_reconciliation.why: Identifies the cases where the winner depends on which data source and which games are counted, which this contract leaves unspecified in the sample.

cbb.leader_average_inertia.label: Leaderboard average inertia and remaining-swing bound
cbb.leader_average_inertia.mechanism: A season average moves by at most (x - mean)/(g+1) per game, so the games remaining bound how far the gap between the leader and challengers can close, and late in the season a lead is close to locked.
cbb.leader_average_inertia.rationale: At 25 games played one 40-point game raises a 20 ppg average by under 0.8, and a challenger 1.5 ppg back needs several far above average games, so the effective uncertainty falls as 1/g; postseason games add few extra samples, which matters most for players on deep-tournament teams.
cbb.leader_average_inertia.measurement: For each pair (leader, challenger) compute the gap in current average, the number of games remaining for each (regular-season schedule plus expected postseason), the per-game sd, and the swing bound d = (mu_challenger - mu_leader) * G_rem/(g+G_rem) plus the standard error sqrt(G_rem) * sd/(g+G_rem). The feature is z = (gap - expected_catch_up)/se. As-of: updated after every game by either player.
cbb.leader_average_inertia.why: Quantifies how much of the leaderboard is already locked in, so early-season and late-season prices are treated with the correct amount of remaining variance.

cbb.stat_leader_race_model.reason: Models the exact event, a maximum over noisy candidate averages with postseason games and thresholds; its inputs need the new qualification and inertia terms.

cbb.player_usage.reason: Usage drives points and threes per game and is persistent; for rebound and assist leaders other drivers matter, so it is only primary for scoring categories.

cbb.player_minutes.reason: Every counting average is minutes times a per-minute rate, so role stability in minutes is the largest driver after talent.

cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.reason: Games missed from different causes have different return probabilities and determine both the average sample and eligibility.

cbb.star_injury_risk.reason: Defined for postseason availability; it captures a valid risk of missing games but is calibrated for tournament games rather than a whole season.

cbb.three_makes_compound_distribution.reason: Directly the compound distribution for the made-threes category, irrelevant for points or rebounds leader markets.

cbb.player_three_volume.reason: Volume of three-point attempts is the main separator for a 3PM leader but applies only to that category.

cbb.rebound_pool.reason: Defines the opportunity pool for rebounds per game, applicable to the rebounds leader markets only.

cbb.assist_conversion_chain.reason: Defines assist opportunity and conversion for assists per game leaders, not other categories.

cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.reason: Many leader candidates are new to their team; a cold-start prior is needed in preseason, fading as games accumulate.

cbb.teammate_absence_shift.reason: Usage redistribution after a teammate absence can lift a candidate's average, important for conference leaders on thin rosters.

cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.reason: Dispersion by role scales the uncertainty of the average; an ingredient for the race simulation more than a mean shifter.

cbb.regular_season_game_inventory.reason: Counts games and official status that form the denominator of the average; mostly fixed by schedules once released.

cbb.tempo.reason: Team pace multiplies opportunity for all counting stats but is already embedded in usage-based per-game projections.

cbb.box_score_source_risk.reason: The final table is only as reliable as its feed; low risk for most players but material when the top two are close.

m.rules_text.reason: Needed for which games count, minimum thresholds and the unseen clause on non-qualification; no predictive content.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Past season settlements indicate the data source and timing used; not a predictor.

interactions.mechanism: Points per game equal minutes times usage-driven per-minute scoring, so a 10 percent rise in each gives about 21 percent more, and teammate departures or injuries can raise both together for a candidate.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress player-season ppg on log minutes and log usage with an interaction and test whether the elasticity of the product is about one for each.

interactions.mechanism: Eligibility requires a minimum share of games, so a candidate with margin of two games above the threshold who misses three loses all probability; the cost of absence is zero until the threshold and then total.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate candidates with and without the filter and compare leader probability for players within 3 games of the minimum.

interactions.mechanism: Early in the season an average moves by up to a point per game and leaders change often; after 25 games it moves by less than a few tenths, so the probability a leader holds rises sharply in the second half of the season.
interactions.how_to_test: Calibrate historical leader probability at game 10, 20 and 30 against the realised leader and check the lead-hold rate by z-score bucket.

interactions.mechanism: Made threes are attempts times a noisy make rate; volume gives a stable base and the make rate adds luck, so the 3PM leader is typically a high-volume shooter whose make rate is not extreme and uncertainty is dominated by the rate for low-volume candidates.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose season 3PM leaders into volume and percentage in past seasons and check which component explains the leader rank change between week 8 and the end.

interactions.mechanism: A leader on a deep-run team gains postseason games that reduce noise but raise injury exposure, and a leader on an early-eliminated team stops accumulating games, so the effect of tournament depth depends on both the quality of opposition and risk of absence.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare changes in per-game average between the end of the regular season and the final for leaders by postseason games played.

nonlinearities.why: Each game's weight in the average falls with games played, so remaining uncertainty collapses and a fixed gap is worth more probability late in the season.
Eligibility is binary; being one game short removes a candidate completely even if his average is the highest.
Starters near the ceiling cannot add much and foul trouble or blowouts cut minutes, so extra role gains saturate for the most used players.
